newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Princess Cristina to marry handball player.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Princess Cristina to marry handball player.

text.p: Spain's Princess Cristina, the youngest daughter of King Juan Carlos and Queen Sofia, will marry professional handball player Inaki Urdangarin in the autumn, the royal palace said on Wednesday.
The 29-year-old athlete will formally ask for Cristina's hand on Saturday, and their wedding will take place later this year in Barcelona where the two live, the royal family said in a statement.

It will be the second wedding for the royal household in the past two years. The King and Queen's eldest daughter, Princess Elena, married Spanish businessman Jaime de Marichalar in a lavish ceremony in spring 1995.
Cristina, 31, met her fiance at the Olympic Games in Atlanta last year when he was a member of Spain's handball team.
Rumours of the wedding started to surface a month ago when the two were spotted together in Barcelona. They have reportedly been dating for the past eight months.
The handsome, blue-eyed athlete from the northern Basque region plays handball for Barcelona and is rated one of the top five Spanish players of all time.

During the Atlanta Games his team won a bronze medal which the 6-foot-5-inch (1.96-m) Urdangarin later physically split in half with an injured team mate who could not attend the Olympics, according to the Spanish media.
The two are united in their love for sport. Cristina is also an athlete and was a member of the Olympic sailing team at the Seoul Games in 1988, where she carried the flag for Spain.
She is an independent, working woman who drives herself to the office each morning at a savings bank in Barcelona, where she works in the photographic department.
Dressed in a black leather jacket and sunglasses, the princess arrived at work on Wednesday to be greeted by a horde of journalists who have been speculating for weeks about her marriage plans.

Her down-to-earth style has helped cement the royal family's place in the hearts of the Spanish public. Unlike the British royals, whose reputation has been damaged by the exploits of younger members, the children of Spain's king and queen have maintained a sense of decorum.

Royal watchers say the Spanish royals are also popular because they are not afraid to show their human side in public. During the 1996 Olympics, Cristina jumped and cheered loudly during Spanish handball matches.
Cristina studied politics at Madrid's Complutense University and went on to get a master's degree in international relations at the University of New York.
To judge from her elder sister Elena's wedding two years ago, the marriage will be a glittering affair.

Elena, wearing an elegant dress with a flowing train and tiara, was married in the cathedral in the southern city of Seville. The ceremony was attended by royalty from around the world and broadcast on television to 400 million viewers.
The youngest member of the family, Crown Prince Felipe, 29, is still single and has given no hint of plans to marry anytime soon.
King Juan Carlos married Queen Sofia in exile in Athens. The royal family was reinstated in 1975 by dictator Francisco Franco after some 40 years in exile.
